comparison: Both strongly support the finding that CIH disrupts swallow motor patterns (C7, C46-C52, C133). OpenEval emphasizes quantitative EMG evidence from Figure 1, while peer reviewers affirm this as a 'core finding' with 'solid results.' Both note the variety of atypical motor patterns in CIH mice versus consistent patterns in normoxic controls.

Complete overlap on claims C65-C69, C125, C153 regarding differential genotype effects. OpenEval finds these claims SUPPORTED by quantitative observations, while peer reviewers rate them UNCERTAIN due to lack of concurrent controls and statistical comparison to normoxic mice. Reviewer 1 questions whether observed phenomena are truly due to CIH given the reliance on historical controls.

Both address phase-dependent effects (C81-C87) and genotype differences (C70-C80). OpenEval finds statistical support via two-way ANOVA and post-hoc tests. Peer reviewers accept the technical rigor and data but find interpretation insufficient, requesting more discussion of viable reasons for genotype differences and known population characteristics.

Both evaluate respiratory rhythm correlations (C88-C96, C127). OpenEval finds strong statistical support via Pearson correlations. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 1 explicitly stating difficulty understanding the functional significance of these correlation analyses, questioning the validity or importance of the claims despite not challenging the statistics.

Both address laryngeal activation patterns (C56-C64, C163-C167). OpenEval supports claims based on quantitative comparisons to published controls. Peer reviewers accept these findings without challenge, noting relevance to respiratory pathophysiology and OSA. The comparison to clinical OSA is accepted by reviewers.

Both support preservation of swallow-breathing coordination (C97-C98, C128-C129). OpenEval emphasizes statistical evidence showing no significant differences. Peer reviewers affirm 'solid results' on coordination and acknowledge the preparation provides valuable timing information, with no challenges to the finding that coordination is preserved while motor patterns are disrupted.

Both address centrally-evoked laryngeal adductor reflex (C138, C141-C142). OpenEval supports the novelty of this finding while noting unclear functional significance (C143). Peer reviewers accept this as part of 'solid results' without disputing the novelty or validity of observing LAR independent of peripheral stimulation.

Both address histological validation and transfection efficiency (C109-C112). OpenEval supports claims based on quantitative data from Figure 4. Peer reviewers implicitly accept these findings, noting 'rigorous and technically remarkable' procedures and acknowledging genetic manipulations as a strength.

Both evaluate mechanistic conclusions about PiCo-SPG dysfunction (C130, C189, C134, C148-C149, C155). OpenEval finds these SUPPORTED by the pattern of preserved coordination with disrupted patterning. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, noting data are 'descriptive in nature' with 'limited mechanistic insight,' requesting additional circuit-level evidence (Fos markers, other nuclei) to support mechanistic claims.

Both address methodological limitations (C120-C121, C169-C176). OpenEval supports the authors' honest acknowledgment of limitations regarding EMG interpretation and anesthesia effects. Peer reviewers accept these limitations while noting the preparation is 'technically challenging' but data remain 'descriptive,' wishing for more mechanistic depth within the constraints.

Partial overlap on genotype-specific effects (C70-C74). OpenEval supports via two-way ANOVA with post-hoc tests. Peer reviewers accept the data quality but request more discussion of genotype differences, suggesting interpretation is insufficient despite technical rigor.

Partial overlap on laryngeal activation probability across genotypes (C77-C80). OpenEval supports via statistical analysis. Peer reviewers accept technical quality but find discussion of genotype differences inadequate.

Partial overlap on respiratory rhythm correlations for non-swallows (C93-C96). OpenEval supports based on Pearson correlations. Peer reviewers question functional significance of correlation analyses, rating UNCERTAIN despite not challenging the statistics.

Both address differences between PiCo-triggered and water-triggered swallows (C99-C101). OpenEval supports via paired t-tests. Peer reviewers accept these findings as part of the coordination analysis without specific challenge.

Both address amplitude differences between swallow types (C102-C104). OpenEval supports via paired t-tests while noting functional significance cannot be determined from EMG alone. Peer reviewers accept without specific challenge.

Partial overlap on laryngeal activation duration (C62-C64). OpenEval supports via mixed-effects ANOVA showing duration scales with stimulation. Peer reviewers accept laryngeal findings without challenge.
Minimal overlap on coordination preservation (C6, C183). OpenEval supports based on statistical analysis. Peer reviewers affirm coordination findings as part of core results.
Partial overlap on primary interpretation of dual PiCo roles (C134, C149). OpenEval supports this interpretation. Peer reviewers question mechanistic conclusions as extending beyond descriptive data.

Minimal overlap on differential effects on neuronal populations (C155). OpenEval supports inference from genotype data. Peer reviewers request more mechanistic evidence beyond descriptive observations.
Minimal overlap on comparison to OSA literature (C166-C167). OpenEval supports based on literature comparison. Peer reviewers accept clinical relevance to OSA without specific critique.

Minimal overlap on functional consequences speculation (C118, C122, C145-C148). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN noting EMG limitations. Peer reviewers question mechanistic claims and request additional evidence.
